assertions.text: Output contains at least 2 separate markdown tables
assertions.evidence: Response contains Table 1: Trial Eligibility, Table 2: Subscription Charge, and Table 3: Cancellation Refund (3 tables total)

assertions.text: A table or note explicitly captures that the free trial is not available on annual plans (not just implied)
assertions.evidence: Table 1 explicitly shows both annual rows with 'Trial Available? = no': 'New annual subscriber | Annual | no | no' and 'New annual loyalty member | Annual | yes | no'

assertions.text: At least one table row demonstrates the loyalty programme discount scenario for annual plan subscribers
assertions.evidence: Table 2 shows 'Annual loyalty member | Annual | yes | no | £86.29' and Table 3 shows 'Annual loyalty mid-year cancel | Annual | yes | no | no | 165 | 365 | £47.28'

assertions.text: The response identifies at least one genuinely underspecified interaction
assertions.evidence: Open Questions section explicitly identifies four underspecified cases: (1) 'Trial-to-annual upgrade...do they: lose the trial and pay immediately, complete the trial first, or is switching blocked during trial?', (2) 'Loyalty status changes mid-cycle...does the discount apply at the *next* renewal only, or is there a partial adjustment mid-cycle?', (3) Cancel during trial distinction, (4) Rounding rule

assertions.text: The annual/loyalty/trial interaction is correctly resolved with a note explaining that they are mutually exclusive
assertions.evidence: Response explicitly states: 'The loyalty-discount × trial interaction is actually simple (they're mutually exclusive — annual has loyalty discounts but no trial, monthly has trial but no loyalty discount). The thornier questions are #1 (mid-trial plan change) and #2 (loyalty status timing).'

assertions.text: Makes clear that the loyalty discount applies to the annual plan only
assertions.evidence: Table 2 shows 'Monthly loyalty member | Monthly | yes | no | £9.99' (same as non-loyalty monthly) while 'Annual loyalty member | Annual | yes | no | £86.29' (discounted from £95.88). Note states: 'The rules give loyalty discounts on annual only.'

assertions.text: The loyalty annual subscriber's prorated cancellation refund is calculated from the discounted price with a visible trace
assertions.evidence: Table 3 row 'Annual loyalty mid-year cancel | Annual | yes | no | no | 165 | 365 | £47.28' with trace provided: '£86.29 × 200/365 = £47.28' (calculated from discounted price, not full £95.88)

assertions.text: Includes a cancellation/refund table or section with concrete rows
assertions.evidence: Table 3: Cancellation Refund contains six concrete scenario rows including 'Cancel during trial', 'Monthly mid-cycle cancel', 'Monthly cancel within 24h of renewal', 'Annual mid-year cancel', 'Annual loyalty mid-year cancel', and 'Annual cancel within 24h of renewal'

assertions.text: The cancellation/refund table includes a loyalty member column to distinguish loyalty vs non-loyalty refund rows
assertions.evidence: Table 3 has explicit 'Loyalty Member' column, with rows 'Annual mid-year cancel | Annual | no |...' and 'Annual loyalty mid-year cancel | Annual | yes |...' showing different refunds (£52.54 vs £47.28)

assertions.text: The '?' suffix is only used on output/expected columns, not on input columns
assertions.evidence: All three tables use '?' only on output columns: Table 1 'Trial Available?', Table 2 'Amount Charged?', Table 3 'Refund?'. Input columns (Plan, Loyalty Member, In Trial, Days Used, Cycle Days) have no '?' suffix
